entities.summary: Ceionius Proculus (b. 250 CE, Rome) was a Roman administrator and military commander who played a significant role in the administration of the Roman Empire during the Late Antiquity period. He held various positions, including aedile and quaestor, and was involved in several military campaigns, including the Roman conquest of Dacia. Ceionius Proculus was also a prominent figure in the Roman Senate, where he was known for his administrative skills and his ability to navigate the complexities of imperial politics. As a result of his efforts, the Roman Empire was able to maintain its territorial integrity and continue to expand its borders. Ceionius Proculus's legacy can be seen in the continued development of the Roman administrative system and the spread of Roman culture throughout the empire. He was a key figure in the Roman Senate, known for his ability to navigate the complexities of imperial politics, and played a significant role in the administration of the Roman Empire during the Late Antiquity period. His work had a lasting impact on the development of the Roman administrative system, and his legacy can still be seen in the modern-day systems of government that have been influenced by ancient Rome.
